summary: Ireland's Department of Foreign Affairs says a Schengen visa is not valid for travel to Ireland, and that whether you need a visa depends on your nationality, the purpose of your visit and how long you plan to stay. Citizens Information says citizens of the EU, the EEA and Switzerland, and of the countries it lists — among them the United States, Canada, Australia and Japan — do not need a visa to land in Ireland; the UK government says British and Irish citizens travel freely between the UK and Ireland under the Common Travel Area. The Immigration Service says the immigration officer decides the stay, up to a maximum of 3 months. Visa-required nationals visiting for 90 days or less apply for a Short Stay ‘C’ visa (€60 single entry).

notes: Travelling from outside the EU, Revenue's duty-free allowances are general goods worth no more than €430 if you are 15 or over (€215 if under 15), plus 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250g of smoking tobacco, 1 litre of spirits or 2 litres of other alcoholic drinks with no more than 22% alcohol, 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer.

Revenue says that if you arrive from outside the EU with certain goods — among them certain foodstuffs (mainly meat, milk, fish or products thereof), medicines, live or dead animals, fish, birds or plants, products of endangered species, and firearms, weapons, fireworks or explosives — you must declare them to a customs officer.

tips.text: The UK government says British and Irish citizens can travel freely between the UK and Ireland under the Common Travel Area, and that some airlines and ferry operators have introduced, or will introduce, a passport-only identification requirement, so check your carrier's requirements. Ireland's Department of Foreign Affairs says a UK visa is not valid for travel to Ireland, except in limited cases under schemes such as the Short Stay Visa Waiver Programme.

Canada's travel advice says road conditions and road safety are generally good in Ireland, but that some roads can be uneven, narrow and winding, particularly in rural areas, and may become hazardous during severe weather conditions.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa or ETA for Ireland?
faq.answer: No. Citizens Information lists the United States of America among the countries whose citizens do not need a visa to land in Ireland. The Immigration Service says the immigration officer places a stamp in your passport that sets out the duration of your stay, which is at the officer's discretion, up to a maximum of 3 months.

faq.question: Can I visit Ireland with a Schengen visa?
faq.answer: No. Ireland's Department of Foreign Affairs says a Schengen visa is not valid for travel to Ireland, and that a UK visa is not valid either, except in limited cases under specific schemes such as the Short Stay Visa Waiver Programme. Chinese nationals living in China and Indian nationals living in India may be eligible for the British Irish Visa Scheme (BIVS).

faq.question: Do I need a UK ETA to travel to Ireland?
faq.answer: No official Irish source we could read requires a UK ETA for travel to Ireland. Ireland's Immigration Service says an ETA cannot be used under its Short-stay Visa Waiver Programme: a national holding a UK ETA and not a UK visa needs a separate Irish visa to travel to Ireland.

faq.question: Do South African citizens need a visa for Ireland?
faq.answer: South Africa is not among the countries Citizens Information lists as not needing a visa to land in Ireland, and it lists South Africa among the countries whose citizens need a valid Irish transit visa when landing in the State. Visa-required nationals visiting for 90 days or less apply for a Short Stay ‘C’ visa (€60 single entry) online through AVATS.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Ireland as a tourist?
faq.answer: The Immigration Service says the immigration officer places a stamp in your passport that sets out the duration and conditions of your stay; the duration is at the officer's discretion, up to a maximum of 3 months. If you arrive with a short stay ‘C’ visa, you must leave before your landing stamp expires.

summary.text: A Schengen visa is not valid for travel to Ireland.
Whether you need a visa depends on: Your nationality The purpose of your visit How long you plan to stay.
Are a citizen of the EU or the EEA (the EU plus Iceland, Norway and Lichtenstein) or Switzerland
Are a citizen of a country listed in the table below.
Canada New Zealand United States of America
British and Irish citizens can continue to travel freely between the UK and Ireland under the Common Travel Area.
The duration of stay permitted is at the discretion of the immigration officer, up to a maximum of 3 months.
If you are a Visa-required national and you would like to visit Ireland for 90 days or less, you will need to apply for a Short Stay ‘C’ Tourist Visa.

faq.schengen-visa-valid.text: A Schengen visa is not valid for travel to Ireland.
A UK visa is not valid for travel to Ireland, except in limited cases under specific schemes such as the Short Stay Visa Waiver Programme (further details below).
Chinese nationals living in China and Indian nationals living in India may be eligible to apply for the British Irish Visa Scheme (BIVS)

faq.uk-eta-needed.text: Please note that an ETA cannot be used to avail of the SSVWP, any National in possession of an ETA and not a UK Visa will need a separate Irish visa if they wish to travel to the State.

faq.south-africa-visa.text: If you are a citizen of one of the following countries, you will need a valid Irish transit visa when landing in the State:
If you are a Visa-required national and you would like to visit Ireland for 90 days or less, you will need to apply for a Short Stay ‘C’ Tourist Visa.
Use the Automated Visa Application and Tracking System (AVATS) to apply for your visa online.

faq.how-long-stay.text: If you are given permission to enter the state, the immigration officer will place a stamp in your passport which sets out the duration and conditions of your stay in the State.

The duration of stay permitted is at the discretion of the immigration officer, up to a maximum of 3 months. If you arrive with a short stay ‘C’ visa, you must leave the country before your landing stamp expires.

tips.cta-nuance.text: British and Irish citizens can continue to travel freely between the UK and Ireland under the Common Travel Area. Some airlines and ferry operators have introduced, or will be introducing, a passport-only identification requirement. Check your carrier’s requirements before departure
A UK visa is not valid for travel to Ireland, except in limited cases under specific schemes such as the Short Stay Visa Waiver Programme (further details below).

tips.rural-driving.text: Road conditions and road safety are generally good. Some roads can be uneven, narrow and winding, particularly in rural areas. These may become hazardous during severe weather conditions.

entryRequirements.passportValidity.text: Your current passport – your current passport must be valid for at least 6 months after the date you plan to leave Ireland

entryRequirements.travelInsurance.text: If your visa is approved, you must have evidence of medical or travel insurance when you arrive at the port of entry (airport or seaport) and must present it to the Immigration Officer on request.
Other useful documents may include: A travel itinerary Proof of sufficient funds Proof of health insurance that covers the duration of your intended stay

entryRequirements.onwardTicket.text: At a minimum, this includes: Your passport Visa (if necessary) Boarding card. Other useful documents may include: A travel itinerary

entryRequirements.proofOfFunds.text: Other useful documents may include: A travel itinerary Proof of sufficient funds

entryRequirements.customs.currencyLimits.text: Carrying cash - If you enter or leave the European Union (EU) at an Irish airport or port carrying cash of €10,000 or more, you must make a declaration to Customs.

The rules about cash declarations apply to movements of cash of €10,000 or more to, or from, the UK, including the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands. These rules do not apply to movements of cash to, or from, Northern Ireland.

entryRequirements.customs.notes.0.text: You can bring in goods free of duty and tax if their combined value is no more than: €430, if you are 15 or over or €215, if you are under 15.
200 cigarettes 100 cigarillos 50 cigars or 250g smoking tobacco.
1 litre of spirits (whiskey, gin, vodka, and so on) or 2 litres of other alcoholic drinks with no more than 22% alcohol
4 litres of wine (still) 16 litres of beer.

entryRequirements.customs.notes.1.text: If you have any of the following goods, you must declare them to a customs officer:

certain foodstuffs (mainly meat, milk, fish or products thereof) products of endangered species protected items of international heritage medicines firearms, weapons, fireworks or explosives live or dead animals, fish, birds or plants

countryFacts.safety.text: Take precautions to reduce the risk of bag-snatching or pickpocketing. Avoid carrying valuables and large amounts of money. Lock your vehicle and park where possible in a secure car park. Most incidents occur in the larger cities.

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: These may become hazardous during severe weather conditions.

countryFacts.driving.text: As a visitor, you can drive on a licence from any state outside the EU/EEA for up to one year, provided it's current and valid.
You can drive in Ireland with a valid EU/EEA licence until it expires and then you must exchange it for an Irish one.

visaTypes.short-stay-c.feeNotes.text: Some applicants are exempt from the requirement to pay the visa fee.
